OMNISIGHT

The discreet AI copilot
that lives in your lens.

A privacy-conscious, multimodal, real-time copilot for meetings and daily work. It listens only with consent, sees only what you choose to share, and answers in a whisper — short, grounded, private — right in your smart-glasses HUD. Built as developer-controlled software, not locked to any one vendor's assistant.

The glasses

Beautiful enough
to wear. Smart enough to keep on.

This is the idea in glass and titanium — a frame you'd choose for how it looks, with the copilot living quietly inside the lens. No bulk. No sci-fi visor. Just presence.

✦ In-lens private HUD✦ Discreet temple camera✦ All-day frame, not a visor✦ Hardware-agnostic software✦ Designed for meetings first

Vision

You stay present.
It keeps up.

Meetings move fast. Notes, names, numbers, and decisions slip away while you're trying to listen. OMNISIGHT is designed to sit quietly at the edge of your vision — capturing only permitted context, retrieving only authorized knowledge, and offering a concise suggestion exactly when you need it.

“Short in the lens.
Longer on phone or desktop.
Never louder than the room.”

01

Tap / Invoke

You decide when it listens or looks. Nothing is continuous by default.

02

Capture permitted context

Speech and selected screen / camera imagery — gated by consent & policy.

03

Interpret

Speech and visuals are fused into a timestamped multimodal event stream.

04

Retrieve authorized context

Permission-aware RAG over your approved notes, docs, and knowledge.

06

One concise line in your lens. Detail waits on your phone.

Priority use case

Meeting Copilot

Live transcription with consent, judgment about when to speak, and the exact words when it matters — plus a clean recap when the meeting ends. Try the prompts:

Should I speak?

Wait — let the budget point land. Jump in on the timeline, not the cost.

SPEAK WAIT DON'T JUMP IN
Decisions · Blockers · Owners · Next steps — tracked live RECAP READY →

Live transcription — with consent

Explicit, revocable consent from participants, a visible capture indicator, and a hard-stop. No covert recording, ever.

Decision & risk tracking

Decisions, blockers, owners, and next steps captured as they happen — not reconstructed from memory afterward.

Deep dive — permission-aware RAG

Ask against your authorized docs mid-meeting. OMNISIGHT respects document ACLs and Entra ID — if you can't open it, it can't quote it.

Presenter mode + Recap

Presenter cues while you present; a recap and action-items draft waiting when you sit down.

Visual Copilot

See it. Snap it.
Understand it.

On-demand camera snapshots and manually triggered screenshots — not continuous by default. OCR plus multimodal fusion reads the whiteboard, the slide, the label, the error on screen, then recalls your approved notes and docs to explain what you're looking at.

AnswerAskExplainChallengeRecallSummarizeActions

Seven modes, one rule: HUD-short in the lens, longer answers on phone or desktop.

Under the lens

Architecture

Hardware-agnostic by design. Device adapters isolate every vendor API, so OMNISIGHT can rally across platforms instead of betting the company on one frame.

Android / Kotlin

On-device capture, consent & policy gate, HUD rendering. Manual screenshots preferred.

Python / FastAPI

WebSocket / WebRTC streaming, timestamped multimodal event bus, session orchestration.

OpenAI Realtime

Low-latency speech + vision for in-the-moment answers.

  • Optional deep reasoning: Claude candidate

Permission-aware RAG

Retrieval scoped by Entra ID + document ACLs. Authorized context only.

Arbiter & Safety

Response arbiter / safety check, audit logs, minimal retention, deletion controls, encrypted transport.

Start here — How to read this brief

There are 3 different products in this brief. They are called Tier A, Tier B, and Tier C. Do NOT quote them as one device. Quote each tier separately.

Tier A — Order first

The Clip

A small clip-on box that clips to any normal glasses. Camera + microphones + battery. No screen. Order 10 units first, test them, then order 100. This proves the idea fast and cheap.

Tier B — The hero product

The Glasses

Real smart glasses with a screen in the lens. This is the main product we want to sell. Quote only: parts list (BOM) + design work (NRE) + mould/tooling cost. Do NOT make tooling and do NOT take tooling money until Tier A demo passes.

Tier C — Price check only

The Pro

Future, high-end glasses with two screens and full AR. Tell us only: is it possible, and roughly what would it cost? DO NOT ORDER. Do not build it. Saying “not possible in 2026–27” is an honest, acceptable answer.

If a part is not in mass production (not being made in large numbers today), has no public datasheet (no public spec sheet anyone can download), or needs a licence from Qualcomm / Sony / a waveguide maker that we do not hold — mark it RED in your quote, explain why in one simple sentence, and suggest the closest part we can order today. Never quietly swap in a different part.

Glasses = eyes + ears + screen only. They see, listen, and show one short line of text.
Phone = brain. The phone does the heavy thinking and connects to the internet.
Cloud = deep brain. Big questions go to the cloud.
Do NOT try to run a big AI model on the glasses. It will get hot, slow, and kill the battery.

What are we building?

The product, in plain words

OMNISIGHT is a meeting + visual copilot — a small helper that lives in your glasses during work. In a meeting it listens only with permission, and shows you one short, private line in your lens at the right moment. When you look at a slide, whiteboard, or document and tap, it takes one photo, reads it, and explains it. It does not record all day. It does not show long text in the lens — long answers go to the phone.

7 simple modes — the user picks one:

1. Answer — give the answer2. Ask — suggest a question3. Explain — explain simply4. Challenge — check if it is true5. Recall — find it in my notes6. Summarize — short recap7. Actions — who does what next

In a meeting, it must do these 5 jobs

  • Should I speak? — shows only: SPEAK or WAIT
  • What do I say? — one short sentence the user can say out loud
  • Smart question — one good question to ask the room
  • Catch me up — if the user stepped out for 2 minutes, 3 short lines on what they missed
  • Track the meeting — decisions made, risks, who owns each task, and next steps

Plus — Veri truth / scam check in the lens: When someone makes a claim, OMNISIGHT checks it and shows only a colour + 8 words or less. ● GREEN = looks true · ● YELLOW = not sure, check · ● RED = likely false / scam. Example: “RED — That price is not on their website.” Never more than 8 words in the lens.

Tier A — Order first · 10 units, then 100

Tier A — The Clip

A tiny box that clips onto the temple (the arm) of normal glasses. It has a camera and microphones. It talks to the phone by Bluetooth. No screen — the phone shows the answer during the test, and later Tier B glasses will show it in the lens. Keep it simple, light, and cheap to change.

Tier C — Feasibility only · Do not order

Tier C — The Pro (future)

Tell us only if this is possible in 2026–27, and a rough price range. Do not build it. Do not quote tooling for it.

  • Two screens (binocular — one in each lens), MicroLED, at least 1280×720 per eye, at least 40° field of view
  • AR2-class chip (the next, stronger Qualcomm AR chip class)
  • 6DoF SLAM (the glasses know exactly where they are in the room, in all directions)
  • Eye tracking (knows where the user is looking) + depth sensor (knows how far things are)

An honest “not possible yet, here is why” is a good answer. A fake “yes” is the worst answer.

Software — what runs where

Software & API the factory must support

API means the set of commands our app uses to talk to the glasses. If these commands are not open to us, our software cannot run — so this section is as important as the parts tables.

On the glasses — ONLY these jobs

  • VAD (voice activity detection — notice when someone starts/stops talking) + wake keyword spotting
  • Capture — record sound + take photos, only when allowed (see Privacy)
  • Encode — shrink sound as Opus, photos as JPEG, video as H.264, so Bluetooth can carry them
  • HUD rendering — draw the one short line of text on the screen (Tier B Display only)
  • LED + privacy logic — run the recording light and Privacy Mode rules below

Nothing else runs on the glasses. No big AI on the device — remember the architecture rule.

Our backend — we build this, you just must not block it

  • Phone app: Android / Kotlin (Apple iOS support via the same open Bluetooth API)
  • Server: Python / FastAPI
  • Live connection: WebSocket / WebRTC (standard live sound + video connections)
  • Fast answers: OpenAI Realtime (fast AI path)
  • Deep answers: a deep-reasoning AI for hard questions + permission-aware RAG (searches only the documents that user is allowed to see — RAG means the AI looks up your own docs before answering)

Data objects — the 6 named packets our system sends

Your firmware/SDK must let these packets pass with their labels attached. In simple words:

  • CaptureEvent — “a capture just happened” (photo or sound started)
  • TranscriptSegment — one short piece of speech turned into text
  • VisualObservation — what the camera photo shows, in words
  • ContextQuery — a question sent to search the user’s allowed documents
  • CopilotSuggestion — the one short answer shown in the lens
  • DeviceAdapter — the translator for each glasses model, so one app works on many glasses

Every capture packet must carry 3 labels: consent_scope (what the user agreed to), timestamp (exact time), and TTL (time-to-live — when this data must delete itself). No label = do not send it.

Speed targets — to TEST, not to promise

Measure these on the real units and report the real numbers. Do not promise them before you measure them.

Mic → phone (sound reaches the phone)≤200 ms
First rough transcript on screen≤1 second
Answer appears in the lens (glance)≤0.8 sec after answer
Photo → answer≤4 seconds
Word errors — quiet room (WER)≤10%
Word errors — noisy café (WER)≤20%

WER = word error rate — out of 100 spoken words, how many the system hears wrong. Lower is better.

Privacy — non-negotiable means: no exceptions

Privacy rules the hardware must obey

  1. The recording LED is hard-wired to the microphone + camera power. If the mic or camera has power, the light is ON. Software can never record with the light off. There is no setting to change this.
  2. 2-second hold = hardware Privacy Mode OFF. Hold the button for 2 seconds and the mic + camera lose power at the hardware level — not just paused in software. Hold again to turn back on.
  3. No covert recording. No hidden mode, no secret recording feature, no way to turn the LED off while recording. If this is not possible in your design, say so now.
  4. No face recognition of strangers. The glasses must never identify people the user does not know. Do not add this feature.
  5. Safe connections: Bluetooth Secure Connections, TLS 1.3 to the server (latest safe internet encryption), AES-256 encryption for stored data (strong lock on saved files).
  6. Signed firmware + secure boot — the glasses only run software signed by us, and check the signature every time they start. No unsigned software can run.
  7. Factory reset wipes everything — all user data, all pairings, all stored sound/photos, fully deleted.
  8. Manual photos over always-on camera. Photos happen when the user taps. Continuous (always-running) camera is NOT the default and must not be built as the default.

Your reply — use this exact checklist

What to quote — reply checklist 1–10

Send your quote in this order, with these 10 items. A quote missing items will be sent back. Prices in USD please, and write the date your prices expire.

  1. BOM for every part — maker name, exact part number, supplier, price at 10 / 100 / 1,000 / 10,000 units, lead time (how long until parts arrive), and MOQ (minimum order quantity) for each part.
  2. Red-flag list — every part that is not in mass production, has no public datasheet, or needs a licence we do not hold — each marked RED, with your closest orderable alternative next to it.
  3. NRE + tooling, separate for Tier A and Tier B — NRE means one-time design/engineering cost. Tooling means moulds and factory setup. Two separate numbers, never mixed into the unit price.
  4. Per-unit assembled price — one finished unit, tested and in its box/packaging, ready to ship. Include testing + packaging in this number.
  5. Timeline with dates — prototype → EVT (first engineering test build) → DVT (design test build) → PVT (small production test build) → mass production. Give a date for each step.
  6. Samples — cost per sample unit and lead time to get samples to California, USA.
  7. Certification plan + cost — for USA / Canada / UK / EU / Australia. Must cover: FCC, CE/UKCA, IC, RCM, Bluetooth SIG, UN38.3, IEC 62133, RoHS / REACH / Prop 65, IPX4 test, EN 50332. Write who does each test and what each costs.
  8. In-the-box list — everything inside the retail box: glasses/clip, case, cable, cloth, papers — item by item.
  9. Warranty / DOA / RMA + spares — warranty length, what happens if a unit is dead on arrival (DOA), how returns/repairs work (RMA), and price + supply plan for spare parts.
  10. One reference product — name one wearable product you have already shipped to real customers that we can check. If this would be your first wearable, write that clearly — honesty will not disqualify you, hiding it will.

Order sequence — how we will buy, step by step

1

Step 1 — Tier A Clip: 10 → test → 100

Build 10 clips. We test them in real meetings. If they pass, we order 100. If they fail, we fix the design first — no big order on a failed test.

2

Step 2 — Tier B engineering samples

Only after the Tier A demo passes do we order Tier B glasses samples. This is also the first moment any tooling discussion starts.

3

Step 3 — Production, only after sign-off

Full production starts only after EVT and DVT are signed off in writing by us. No tooling money before Step 2. No exceptions.

5 questions you MUST answer in writing

Put these 5 answers on page 1 of your reply. Short, clear answers. “We will check later” is not an answer.

  1. AR1 chip: What is your exact access route to the Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 — your licence, your ODM partner, or distribution? Who signs it?
  2. Waveguide screen: Who is your waveguide supplier, and what are the real, measured field of view, brightness, and light leakage numbers?
  3. Hard-wired LED: Yes or no — can you hard-wire the recording LED to mic/camera power, so software can never record with the light off?
  4. Thinnest temple: What is the thinnest temple (glasses arm) you can build that still fits the mic + speaker + battery stack? Give the number in mm.
  5. Open Bluetooth API: Yes or no — will you give us an open BLE API + SDK so our own app can access mic, camera, and display?

Clear limits

What this is NOT

Not a VR headset

No big screens covering the eyes, no gaming headset. These are normal-looking glasses for work.

Not a hidden recorder

The LED is the product’s promise. Removing the LED ends the project. We will not build a secret recording device.

Not a medical device

No health claims, no diagnosis, no medical use. Do not certify or market it as medical.

Not locked to one AI

Not locked to one AI model or one cloud. Our DeviceAdapter design must let us change AI providers without changing hardware.

AI routing + RAG

Fast-path realtime routing, optional deep reasoning, and permission-aware retrieval wired together.

WEEKS 8–10

Proactive meeting intelligence

SPEAK / WAIT judgment, smart questions, catch-me-up, and decision tracking tuned in live meetings.

WEEKS 10–12

Pilot + hardening

Real-user pilot. Latency, battery, privacy, and answer quality measured — no unmeasured claims.

Privacy by design

Consent isn't a setting.
It's the architecture.

Explicit, revocable consent

Capture starts only with consent — and consent can be withdrawn instantly, by anyone in the room.

Visible indicator + hard-stop

A capture indicator others can see, and a hard-stop that ends capture immediately. No covert recording.

Manual over continuous

Manually triggered screenshots and on-demand snapshots preferred. Continuous capture is not the default.

Encrypted & minimal

Encrypted transport, minimal retention, and real deletion controls — not retention by inertia.

Permission-aware knowledge

Entra ID and document ACLs govern retrieval. OMNISIGHT can only surface what you're authorized to see.

Auditable

Audit logs for capture and retrieval, so trust can be verified — not just promised.

Honest status

Questions, answered plainly.

Is OMNISIGHT a shipped product? +

No. OMNISIGHT is a working blueprint dated November 14, 2026 — vision, use cases, and system architecture defined, with feasibility still to be validated hands-on. This site exists to fund that validation and to rally the manufacturers whose hardware it will run on.

Why not just use the assistant built into the glasses? +

OMNISIGHT is developer-controlled software, not dependent on a vendor's built-in assistant. That independence is the point: one copilot, with your permissions and your knowledge, that can move across frames as hardware evolves.

Which hardware will it run on first? +

RayNeo X3 Pro is the primary prototype candidate and Brilliant Labs Halo is the parallel candidate (ordered Oct 12, 2026). Even Realities G2, Vuzix Z100, Mentra, and XREAL are also under evaluation. The primary path will be chosen on SDK proof-of-concept evidence in Weeks 2–4 — not before.

What does the Testing Round actually fund? +

Prototype testing and hardware validation across six platforms, SDK proof-of-concepts, the 12-week MVP build, and a real-user pilot where latency, battery, privacy, and answer quality are measured. No unmeasured performance claims are made anywhere on this site.

How does privacy work in a real meeting? +

Explicit revocable consent, a visible capture indicator, a hard-stop, manual screenshots preferred over continuous capture, encrypted transport, minimal retention, deletion controls, audit logs, and retrieval governed by Entra ID and document ACLs. No covert recording.

I'm a manufacturer — what does “join hands” mean concretely? +

Provide dev kits, SDK access, an engineering contact, and prototype pricing — and co-build with us. In return, OMNISIGHT aims to become a flagship software layer that gives your hardware an all-day use case: the meeting copilot professionals reach for every morning.

Where are the downloadable blueprint & manufacturing files? +

Right here — in the Documents section, in the top nav (“Documents — Blueprint + Build MD”), under the hero buttons, and at the top of the Build It brief. Two files: and — both open in the premium reader on this page. Raw .md files for forwarding: ⬇ Blueprint .md · ⬇ Manufacturing .md.

I want to build it — where is the full technical brief? +

Read right here in the premium reader, ⬇ download the raw .md file if you need to forward it, or read the same complete brief on-page in Build It — Complete Manufacturer Brief. It is written in simple language for any factory — in China, the USA (including a design partner like 3M), or any qualified ODM. It covers Tier A Clip (order 10, then 100), Tier B Glasses (quote BOM + NRE + tooling only), and Tier C Pro (feasibility only), plus the full parts tables, privacy rules, the 1–10 quote checklist, and the 5 questions every manufacturer must answer in writing.

Doc 1 · Functional BlueprintNov 14, 2026Working blueprint

Full Functional Blueprint

Short in the lens. Longer on phone or desktop. Never louder than the room. A privacy-conscious, multimodal, real-time copilot — hardware-agnostic, developer-controlled, not locked to one vendor, frame, AI model or cloud.

Meeting Copilot — The 5 Jobs

Should I Speak?

SPEAK / WAIT / DON'T JUMP IN — e.g. “Wait — let Maya finish. Your data point lands stronger after hers.”

What Do I Say?

One grounded sentence you can say verbatim.

Smart Question

The question that moves the room, before the moment passes.

Catch Me Up

3 lines if you stepped out ~2 minutes. Plus live Decisions / Risks / Actions tracking, Presenter Mode and Recap.

The 7 Modes

1 Answer2 Ask3 Explain4 Challenge (Veri)5 Recall6 Summarize7 Actions

Veri check: GREEN = looks true · YELLOW = not sure, check · RED = likely false/scam — colour + ≤8 words in the lens only.

API Objects — 6 named packets

CaptureEventTranscriptSegmentVisualObservationContextQueryCopilotSuggestion (expiry + uncertainty)DeviceAdapter

Every capture packet carries consent_scope + timestamp + TTL. No label = do not send it.
